news.title: FIFA's controversial bid to sell the World Cup to a Trump associate
news.lede: Gianni Infantino has proposed selling off the global football governing body's events and competitions arm to private investors. (Reuters: Dylan Martinez). Gianni Infantino's $US20 billion ($28.7 billion) proposal to sell stakes in FIFA's events and competitions arm to corporate investors has drawn condemnation from football's international organising confederations. On Tuesday the FIFA president announced a bid to form a commercial subsidiary called FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) that would grant private buyers control over competitions including the World Cup and Club World Cup.

news.title: World game at war: why some European nations have threatened a World Cup boycott
news.lede: A little over a week since the 2026 men’s World Cup final, world soccer appears on the brink of war. The main battleground is a proposal from FIFA president Gianni Infantino to sell off a key function of the not-for-profit association. It has even led to a threat from some European nations to boycott upcoming World Cups. So, why is Infantino’s proposal so controversial and why are so many nations against the plan?

news.title: World Cup 2026: When the spectator became the product
news.lede: The 2026 World Cup exposed how modern sport increasingly treats fans not as spectators, but as products whose attention is constantly being sold, writes Jack Waters. I’D BEEN LOOKING FORWARD to this year’s World Cup for months. As a lifelong football fan, it’s always been one of those rare events that lets me completely switch off from the world and tune into the game I’ve grown up on. But this tournament was different.

news.title: Uefa to hold emergency meeting over Fifa World Cup plans
news.lede: Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin will lead an emergency meeting of all 55 member associations on Thursday. Uefa will hold an emergency meeting on Thursday afternoon to discuss its response to the controversial World Cup stakeholder plans proposed by Fifa and its president Gianni Infantino. European football's governing body kept up its offensive over the plans after it was discovered Fifa had sent a letter, seen by the BBC, to all 211 member associations giving them until 19 September to decide if they want to accept the deal, and with it the first $20m (£15m) of an initial $40m (£30m). "We have learned of Fifa's deadline to associations to support their proposals or have the one-off payout offer withdrawn," said Uefa.

news.title: Infantino's greed has football on brink 60 years on from England's greatest day
news.lede: THE World Cup used to be so simple — and today serves as the perfect reminder of that. It was exactly 60 years ago that Bobby Moore was lifting the Jules Rimet trophy and being hoisted on the shoulders of his England team-mates. Those iconic scenes at Wembley came after a tournament that had just 16 teams and lasted only 20 days. There were no hydration breaks or half-time shows and certainly no private investors looking for a slice of the pie.

news.title: Infantino defends plan to sell World Cup stakes but could Uefa launch boycott?
news.lede: Fifa President Gianni Infantino called the plan to sell stakes in the World Cup a proposal but “not an obligation” after the idea provoked a furious response from football authorities. Fifa announced plans this week to create a $20 billion subsidiary to run the World Cup and its other events, ⁠and said it will offer stakes of up to ​20 per cent ⁠in it to ‌external investors. The proposal drew strong criticism from the ​sport's regional confederations, who said they were blindsided by the plan from the world governing body. But Infantino said strengthening the commercial side of the game is the natural next step in this evolution.

news.title: Disgraced soccer figures apologize for World Cup group stage elimination
news.lede: Disgraced soccer figures on Thursday apologized for the South Korean men's national team's group stage elimination from the World Cup. They were summoned to a parliamentary hearing on alleged corruption in the Korea Football Association, including its head coach hiring process. The figures in the hearing, however, denied allegations of nepotism linked to Hong Myung-bo's controversial appointment as head coach of the men's national football team in 2024. At the hearing held by the National Assembly's Culture, Sports and Tourism Committee, former KFA chair Chung Mong-gyu said, "I am sorry for the series of controversies and the poor performance in the 2026 World Cup."

news.title: Messi returns to MLS training 10 days after World Cup final heartbreak
news.lede: Lionel Messi returns to Inter Miami after Argentina's World Cup final defeat by Spain, which led to retirement rumours.
